key_insight: A shallow, hardware-aware QAOA pipeline can run real honeypot traffic partitioning workloads on IBM quantum processors, but performance is strongly shaped by backend architecture and routing overhead.
engineering_relevance: The paper provides a reproducible benchmark framework for evaluating quantum optimization on cybersecurity traffic segregation problems, with separate reporting for objective quality, security metrics, routing cost, and runtime.
method: Mapped honeypot traffic partitioning to a weighted MaxCut/QUBO formulation.
Ran fixed-depth QAOA on IBM quantum hardware and compared against classical heuristics and a noiseless MPS reference.
Evaluated labeled temporal bipartite benchmark graphs at 16, 32, 66, and 110 nodes across multiple backends.
evidence_signal: The largest benchmark used a 110-node, 181-edge instance executed on three IBM backends, and the authors report that simple classical heuristics still solve the current labeled graphs.
watch_item: This is not a quantum advantage result; the main caution is that hardware connectivity and routing overhead can materially change observed solution quality and runtime.
paper_title: Hardware-Aware QAOA for Honeypot Traffic Partitioning on 100+ Qubit IBM Quantum Processors
